prompt:
More and more adults around the world are choosing to learn a foreign language.

Why do people want to learn a foreign language? What is the most effective way to learn one?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
checklist: Answer question 1: explain why adults want to learn a foreign language
Answer question 2: identify THE most effective way (a clear choice, not just a list)
Justify why that method is the most effective
Support both answers with explanation and examples
Give both questions roughly equal attention

for: Q1: career advancement and international job opportunities
Q1: travel, studying abroad or emigrating
Q1: connecting with family, partners or friends from other cultures
Q1: personal challenge, keeping the brain active, interest in another culture
against: Q2: immersion (living or studying in the country) forces constant practice
Q2: regular conversation with native speakers or language exchanges
Q2: combining structured classes with daily exposure (films, podcasts, reading)
Q2: short daily practice is better than occasional long sessions

models.text:
Language schools and learning apps report growing numbers of adult students, many of whom have not studied a language since school. Their motives are varied, but most fall into professional and personal categories. As for method, I would argue that regular, meaningful interaction with speakers of the language is the single most effective approach.

The most common motivation is undoubtedly professional. In a globalised economy, employees who can negotiate with clients or read documents in a second language are more valuable, and in many companies English, Mandarin or Spanish has become a requirement for promotion. Others have more personal reasons. Some are planning to study, work or retire abroad and know that daily life will be far easier if they can speak to neighbours and officials. Many adults also learn a language in order to communicate with a partner's family or to reconnect with their own heritage, while a growing number simply enjoy the intellectual challenge, encouraged by evidence that learning new skills helps to keep the brain healthy in later life.

When it comes to learning effectively, textbooks and apps certainly have their place, particularly for building vocabulary and understanding grammar. However, a language is above all a tool for communication, and the decisive factor is how often learners actually use it. Speaking regularly with native or fluent speakers forces them to understand natural, unscripted speech, to retrieve words under pressure and to notice the gaps in their knowledge. This can be achieved through full immersion, such as living with a host family, but it does not require moving abroad: online tutors and local language exchanges now make conversation practice accessible to almost anyone. An adult who talks with a partner for thirty minutes three times a week will typically progress far faster than one who only completes grammar exercises.

In conclusion, adults learn languages mainly for their careers, for travel and relationships, and for personal satisfaction. Whatever their reason, frequent real communication is the most efficient path to fluency.
models.commentary: Task Response (8): responde a las dos preguntas con desarrollo equilibrado y, en la segunda, elige claramente UN método ('regular, meaningful interaction') y lo justifica, en lugar de enumerar opciones. Ejemplos concretos (intercambio 30 minutos tres veces por semana). Coherence & Cohesion (8): un párrafo por pregunta, con la respuesta anticipada en la introducción; 'When it comes to', 'However', 'This can be achieved' hacen avanzar el razonamiento. Lexical Resource (8): léxico preciso ('heritage', 'unscripted speech', 'retrieve words under pressure', 'full immersion', 'host family'). Grammatical Range & Accuracy (8): estructuras variadas (relativas 'many of whom', comparativas, pasivas) sin errores. Para un 9: un párrafo de cuerpo por pregunta está bien, pero el segundo podría reconocer brevemente los límites de la inmersión para mostrar un razonamiento aún más matizado.

models.text:
Nowadays, many adults decide to study a foreign language, even after they have finished their formal education. There are several reasons for this, and in my opinion the best way to learn a language is to practise speaking it as much as possible with real people.

There are different reasons why adults learn foreign languages. The main one is work. Many companies operate internationally, so employees who speak English or another language have better chances of getting a good job or a promotion. For example, in Spain, people who speak English and German can find jobs in tourism more easily. Another reason is travel. When people visit other countries, they want to communicate with local people, order food and understand the culture better. Finally, some people learn a language for personal reasons, such as having a foreign partner or simply enjoying the challenge of learning something new.

In my opinion, the most effective way to learn a language is to speak it regularly. Many people study grammar for years at school, but they still cannot have a simple conversation, because they never practise. When learners talk with native speakers, they hear the natural pronunciation and learn useful everyday expressions. They also become more confident. Living in the country is the ideal situation, but people who cannot travel can use language exchange websites or join conversation groups in their city.

In conclusion, adults learn foreign languages mainly for work, travel and personal reasons. I believe that the most effective method is to practise speaking with other people, because it improves both fluency and confidence.
models.commentary: Task Response (7): responde a ambas preguntas y elige un método claro; el ejemplo de España es concreto. La segunda parte está algo menos desarrollada (no explica en profundidad por qué hablar acelera el aprendizaje). Coherence & Cohesion (7): estructura clara (un párrafo por pregunta); conectores correctos pero formulaicos ('The main one', 'Another reason', 'Finally'). Lexical Resource (7): vocabulario adecuado ('operate internationally', 'promotion', 'language exchange', 'fluency'), con expresiones algo generales ('a good job', 'better chances'). Grammatical Range & Accuracy (7): buen control de frases complejas; errores casi inexistentes. Para subir a 8: desarrollar el mecanismo de por qué funciona el método (recuperar palabras bajo presión, detectar lagunas), añadir algún matiz y usar léxico más variado.

models.text:
Today, many adults want to learn a new language like English, Chinese or French. In this essay I will explain why they want to learn and what is the best way to learn a language.

Firstly, there are many reasons for learn a language. The most important reason is the work. Nowadays the companies are international and they need workers who can speak English. If you speak English, you can have a better job and a better salary. Also, people like to travel to other countries and when they speak the language they can talk with the people and they can enjoy more the travel. Some people also learn languages because they like the culture of other country, for example the Japanese culture or the Korean music.

Secondly, there are many ways to learn a language. Some people go to a language school, other people use apps in the mobile phone like Duolingo, and other people watch films and series in the original version. I think all these ways are good. But in my opinion the best way is to go to live in the country. When you live in the country you need to speak the language every day in the supermarket, in the bank and with your friends, so you learn very fast. My friend lived in London for one year and now she speaks English very good.

In conclusion, people learn languages for the work, the travel and the culture. The best way to learn is to live in the country but if you can not do this, you can go to a school or use apps.
models.commentary: Task Response (6): responde a ambas preguntas y acaba eligiendo un método (vivir en el país), pero antes dice 'all these ways are good', lo que debilita la respuesta a 'the most effective way'. Las ideas son generales y el ejemplo de la amiga es anecdótico. Coherence & Cohesion (6): estructura clara, pero 'Firstly' y 'Secondly' introducen preguntas, no argumentos; 'Also' y 'other people' se repiten. Lexical Resource (6): vocabulario básico ('better job', 'very fast', 'enjoy more the travel'); 'the travel' no es natural (travelling / the trip). Grammatical Range & Accuracy (6): errores frecuentes: 'what is the best way' en pregunta indirecta (what the best way is), 'for learn', 'other country' (other countries), 'speaks English very good' (well), 'enjoy more the travel' (orden), artículos innecesarios ('the work'). Para subir a 7: responder a la segunda pregunta de forma directa desde el principio, justificar el método con un razonamiento y no sólo una anécdota, y revisar preguntas indirectas, adverbios y artículos.

prompt:
In many countries, famous entertainers and sports stars earn far more money than doctors, nurses and teachers.

Why is this the case? Do you think this situation should be changed?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
checklist: Answer question 1: explain WHY celebrities earn more than doctors, nurses and teachers
Answer question 2: give a clear yes/no opinion on whether this should change
If you think it should change, say how (or explain why it cannot/should not)
Support both answers with explanation and examples
Give both questions roughly equal attention

for: Q1: market forces: millions of fans, TV rights, advertising and ticket sales generate huge revenues
Q1: top talent is rare; only a few people can perform at the highest level
Q1: careers in sport and entertainment are short and uncertain
Q1: public-sector salaries are set by governments with limited budgets
against: Q2 (yes): essential workers' pay should reflect their value to society; shortages of nurses and teachers
Q2 (yes): higher taxes on very high incomes could fund public salaries
Q2 (no): governments cannot easily cap private earnings; fans freely choose to pay
Q2 (partly): raise public-sector pay rather than reduce celebrities' income

models.text:
It is a striking feature of modern economies that a footballer may earn more in a week than a nurse earns in several years. This disparity is largely the result of how markets reward scarce talent and mass audiences. In my view, while celebrities' incomes cannot realistically be limited, the pay and status of essential public servants should certainly be improved.

The main explanation lies in the economics of entertainment. A world-class footballer or pop singer attracts millions of paying fans, and their performances generate enormous revenue through ticket sales, broadcasting rights, streaming and advertising. Clubs and record companies are willing to pay these individuals huge sums because they bring in even larger profits. Their talent is also extremely rare, and their careers are often short and unpredictable, which further increases what they can demand. Doctors, nurses and teachers, by contrast, are mostly employed by the state, so their salaries are determined not by the value they create but by public budgets, which are constrained by taxation and competing priorities.

I believe the situation should change, but in a particular way. Attempting to cap the earnings of entertainers would be both impractical and arguably unfair, since people voluntarily choose to spend their money on concerts and matches. However, the low pay of essential workers has real consequences. Many countries now face serious shortages of nurses and teachers, as talented young people choose better-paid careers and experienced staff leave the profession. The pandemic demonstrated how much society depends on healthcare workers, yet in many places their wages have barely risen. Governments should therefore make these professions more attractive through higher salaries, funded if necessary by more progressive taxation of the highest incomes, including those of celebrities.

In conclusion, entertainers earn more because they generate vast commercial revenue, whereas public servants are paid from limited state budgets. Rather than reducing celebrities' incomes, societies should ensure that those who keep them healthy and educated are properly rewarded.
models.commentary: Task Response (8): responde a las dos preguntas de forma directa y matizada: explica el porqué con argumentos económicos sólidos y da una opinión clara ('should change, but in a particular way'), con una propuesta concreta (subir salarios públicos mediante impuestos progresivos). Coherence & Cohesion (8): la introducción anticipa ambas respuestas; 'by contrast', 'However', 'therefore' estructuran el razonamiento con naturalidad. Lexical Resource (8): léxico preciso ('disparity', 'scarce talent', 'broadcasting rights', 'constrained by', 'progressive taxation', 'public servants'). Grammatical Range & Accuracy (8): gran variedad (comparativas, 'not by... but by', pasivas, participio 'funded if necessary by') sin errores. Para un 9: un ejemplo aún más concreto (cifras o un país con escasez documentada) y algo más de reflexión sobre el valor social frente al valor de mercado.

models.text:
In most countries, famous actors, singers and athletes earn much higher salaries than people in important professions such as medicine and education. There are several reasons for this, and I believe that the situation should change, at least partly.

The first reason is that celebrities make a lot of money for other people. For example, a famous football player attracts thousands of fans to the stadium and millions of viewers on television, so clubs, TV channels and sponsors earn huge profits. Because of this, they are happy to pay the player a very high salary. Secondly, there are very few people who have the talent to become a top star, while there are many qualified teachers and nurses. Finally, most doctors, nurses and teachers work for the government, and their salaries depend on the public budget, which is limited.

In my opinion, this situation is unfair and should be changed. Doctors and nurses save lives, and teachers educate the next generation, so their work is much more important for society than entertainment. If their salaries are low, fewer young people will choose these careers. In fact, many countries already have a shortage of nurses. However, I do not think the government should limit the salaries of celebrities, because fans decide to spend their money freely. Instead, governments should increase the salaries of public workers, perhaps by taxing very rich people more.

In conclusion, celebrities earn more because they generate a lot of money and their talent is rare. I believe that governments should pay essential workers better, because they make a greater contribution to society.
models.commentary: Task Response (7): responde a ambas preguntas con una opinión clara y una propuesta razonable. Algún argumento es discutible sin matizar ('there are many qualified teachers and nurses' choca con la escasez que menciona después). Coherence & Cohesion (7): estructura clara y lógica; conectores correctos pero enumerativos ('The first reason', 'Secondly', 'Finally'). Lexical Resource (7): vocabulario adecuado ('sponsors', 'huge profits', 'shortage', 'essential workers'), con expresiones generales ('a lot of money', 'very rich people'). Grammatical Range & Accuracy (7): buena variedad (condicionales, relativas, 'Instead'); errores mínimos. Para subir a 8: evitar contradicciones internas, desarrollar la consecuencia de la escasez con más detalle y precisar el léxico ('progressive taxation', 'revenue', 'broadcasting rights').

models.text:
Nowadays, the famous people like footballers, singers and actors earn a lot of money, much more than doctors or teachers. In this essay I will explain why this happen and if it should change.

There are some reasons why celebrities earn more money. First, they are very popular and many people want to see them. For example, Cristiano Ronaldo has millions of followers in Instagram and the companies pay him a lot of money for advertising their products. Also the people pay for tickets to go to the concerts and the football matches. Second, the doctors and the teachers work for the government and the government don't have much money, so the salaries are low.

In my opinion, this situation should change. The doctors and the nurses are very important because they save the life of the people. During the Covid, they worked very hard and many of them got sick. The teachers are also very important because they teach the children and the children are the future of the country. But the footballers only play a game and the singers only sing, this is not so important for the society.

I think the government should pay more money to the doctors and the teachers. Also the government should put more taxes to the celebrities, because they have too much money and they don't need all this money.

In conclusion, celebrities earn more money because they are popular and the companies pay them a lot. I think this is not fair and the government should change this situation and pay more to the important workers.
models.commentary: Task Response (6): responde a ambas preguntas con una opinión clara, pero las razones son superficiales y el tono es a veces poco académico ('the footballers only play a game'). La propuesta final se enuncia sin explicar cómo funcionaría. Coherence & Cohesion (6): estructura correcta, pero conectores mecánicos ('First', 'Second', 'Also'); falta progresión dentro de los párrafos. Lexical Resource (6): vocabulario limitado y repetitivo ('a lot of money' aparece muchas veces, 'very important'); colocaciones incorrectas ('followers in Instagram' → on, 'put more taxes to' → impose higher taxes on, 'save the life of the people'). Grammatical Range & Accuracy (6): errores frecuentes: 'why this happen', 'if it should change' (whether), 'the government don't', 'During the Covid', 'this is not so important for the society'; un 'comma splice' ('only sing, this is...'). Para subir a 7: explicar las causas con lógica económica (ingresos que generan), mantener un registro académico y ampliar el vocabulario para evitar repeticiones.

prompt:
In most countries, people are living much longer than they did in the past, and the proportion of older people in the population is increasing.

What can individuals do to prepare for a long old age? What responsibilities should governments have towards elderly citizens?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
checklist: Answer question 1: what INDIVIDUALS can do to prepare for old age (finance, health, social life)
Answer question 2: what GOVERNMENTS should be responsible for
Give specific, realistic suggestions rather than vague statements
Support both answers with explanation and examples
Give both questions roughly equal attention

for: Individuals: save and invest for retirement from an early age
Individuals: maintain physical health through exercise and diet
Individuals: keep learning and stay socially connected to avoid isolation
Individuals: plan housing that will remain suitable as mobility declines
against: Governments: guarantee a basic pension that prevents poverty
Governments: provide affordable healthcare and long-term care
Governments: adapt cities (transport, accessible buildings) for older people
Governments: support flexible retirement and protect older workers from discrimination

models.text:
Thanks to advances in medicine and living standards, many people can now expect to live well into their eighties or nineties. A longer life is a remarkable achievement, but it brings financial, physical and social challenges that both individuals and governments need to prepare for.

Individuals have a responsibility to plan ahead, and the earlier they start, the better. Financially, this means saving regularly from their first years of employment, since even modest contributions to a pension fund grow considerably over four decades. Health is equally important: habits such as regular exercise, a balanced diet and not smoking do not merely extend life but increase the number of years lived free from disability. Perhaps less obviously, people should invest in their social and mental well-being. Loneliness is a major problem among the elderly, and those who maintain friendships, take part in community activities or continue learning new skills tend to remain healthier and happier. Practical decisions also matter; for instance, choosing a home without steep stairs can allow someone to live independently for longer.

Nevertheless, individual effort has limits, and the state must provide a safety net. The most basic duty of government is to guarantee a pension that keeps every older citizen out of poverty, regardless of how much they were able to save. Governments should also ensure access to affordable healthcare and long-term care, which families can rarely afford alone; Japan's compulsory care insurance, introduced in 2000, is one model that spreads these costs across society. In addition, public authorities can make cities more age-friendly by providing accessible transport, benches and step-free buildings, and they can encourage employers to offer flexible or part-time work to those who wish to retire gradually.

In conclusion, preparing for a long old age requires individuals to look after their finances, health and relationships, while governments must provide adequate pensions, care and suitable public spaces. Only through this shared responsibility can longer lives also be good lives.
models.commentary: Task Response (8): responde a las dos preguntas con desarrollo amplio y equilibrado; las sugerencias son específicas (pensiones desde el primer empleo, vivienda sin escaleras, seguro de dependencia de Japón) y abarcan finanzas, salud y vida social. Coherence & Cohesion (8): un párrafo por pregunta; 'Nevertheless, individual effort has limits' enlaza las dos partes de forma lógica; buen uso de 'Perhaps less obviously', 'Practical decisions also matter'. Lexical Resource (8): léxico preciso ('safety net', 'free from disability', 'long-term care', 'age-friendly', 'step-free'). Grammatical Range & Accuracy (8): estructuras variadas ('the earlier... the better', 'not merely... but', inversión 'Only through... can') sin errores. Para un 9: párrafos algo menos densos (dividir cada respuesta en dos subideas bien separadas) y una reflexión breve sobre la sostenibilidad del sistema de pensiones.

models.text:
People today live much longer than in the past, and in many countries there are more and more elderly people. This situation means that both individuals and governments need to prepare for a long old age.

First of all, individuals should take care of their finances. When people retire, their income usually falls, so it is important to save money while they are still working. For example, they can pay into a private pension plan or buy a house that they will own completely by the time they retire. Secondly, people should look after their health. Doing regular exercise, eating healthy food and having regular medical check-ups can help them stay active and independent for longer. Finally, it is important to keep an active social life. Many old people feel lonely, especially after their children leave home, so hobbies, volunteering or clubs can help them stay happy and connected.

Governments also have important responsibilities towards elderly citizens. The most important one is to provide a pension, so that old people who did not save enough money can still live with dignity. In addition, governments should offer good healthcare, because older people usually need more medical treatment. For instance, in Spain, public healthcare is free, which is a great help for pensioners. Governments should also build care homes and support families who look after their elderly relatives.

In conclusion, individuals should save money, stay healthy and keep socially active to prepare for old age. At the same time, governments must provide pensions, healthcare and care services so that all elderly people can have a good quality of life.
models.commentary: Task Response (7): responde a ambas preguntas con ideas relevantes y algún ejemplo (sanidad pública en España). La parte de los gobiernos es algo más breve y general ('support families' sin explicar cómo). Coherence & Cohesion (7): organización clara; conectores enumerativos y algo mecánicos ('First of all', 'Secondly', 'Finally', 'In addition'). Lexical Resource (7): vocabulario adecuado ('pension plan', 'check-ups', 'live with dignity', 'care homes'), aunque 'old people' se repite y sería mejor alternarlo con 'elderly people', 'older citizens'. Grammatical Range & Accuracy (7): frases complejas correctas ('by the time they retire', 'so that'); errores muy escasos. Para subir a 8: desarrollar más la responsabilidad del gobierno con medidas concretas (ciudades accesibles, jubilación flexible), variar el léxico y reducir la dependencia de conectores ordinales.

models.text:
Nowadays the people live more years than before because the medicine is better. So there are many old people in the society. In this essay I will explain what people can do to prepare for the old age and what the government should do.

Firstly, people need to prepare for the old age. The most important thing is the money. When you are old you don't work, so you need to save money when you are young. If you don't save, you will have problems to pay the bills. Also, people need to do sport and eat healthy food, because if you are healthy you can enjoy more your old age. For example, my grandfather goes to walk every day and he is eighty years old and very healthy.

Secondly, the government have responsibility for the old people. The government must to give a pension to all the old people, because some of them don't have money. Also the hospitals must be free for the old people, because they are sick more often than the young people. Another thing is that the government can build more residences for old people who live alone and they can not take care of themselves.

In my opinion, the family is also important. In my country the children take care of their parents when they are old, and I think this is better than a residence.

In conclusion, the people need to save money and be healthy for the old age, and the government must give pensions and free hospitals to the old people. If everybody help, the old people will have a good life.
models.commentary: Task Response (6): responde a ambas preguntas, pero con ideas básicas y poco desarrolladas; el párrafo sobre la familia no responde a ninguna de las dos preguntas y le resta foco. El ejemplo del abuelo es anecdótico. Coherence & Cohesion (6): estructura identificable pero mecánica ('Firstly', 'Secondly', 'Also', 'Another thing is that'); cambia entre 'you' y 'people', lo que reduce la cohesión. Lexical Resource (6): vocabulario limitado y repetitivo ('the old people' constantemente, 'the money'); 'residences' es un falso amigo (care homes); 'goes to walk' (goes for a walk). Grammatical Range & Accuracy (6): errores frecuentes: 'problems to pay' (paying), 'enjoy more your old age' (orden), 'the government have', 'must to give', 'If everybody help'; exceso de 'the' con sentido general ('the people', 'the medicine', 'the old age'). Para subir a 7: eliminar el párrafo irrelevante, desarrollar cada sugerencia con su porqué, usar sinónimos ('elderly', 'older citizens', 'retirees') y corregir artículos y modales.

prompt:
Today, the same international brands of shops, restaurants and clothing can be found in cities all over the world.

Is this a positive or negative development?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
checklist: State clearly whether you think this is a positive or negative development (or mainly one or the other)
Explain the positive aspects
Explain the negative aspects
Support ideas with explanation and examples
Keep your judgement consistent and restate it in the conclusion

for: Consumers get reliable quality, safety standards and lower prices
Multinationals create jobs and bring investment and training
Travellers and migrants find familiar products abroad
Global brands can spread higher labour or environmental standards
against: Cities lose their unique character; high streets look the same everywhere
Small local businesses cannot compete and close
Profits leave the local economy and go to foreign headquarters
Traditional food, crafts and fashion may disappear

models.text:
A traveller walking through the main shopping street of Madrid, Seoul or Dubai today will see many of the same names: the same coffee chains, fast-food restaurants and fashion retailers. Although this globalisation of brands offers some genuine benefits, I believe it is, on balance, a negative development, because it erodes the distinctive character and economic independence of local communities.

It would be wrong to deny the advantages. International chains generally offer consistent quality, clear hygiene standards and competitive prices, which consumers clearly value; otherwise these companies would not have expanded so successfully. They also create jobs, often providing young people with their first employment and formal training. For tourists and foreign residents, a familiar shop or café can be reassuring in an unfamiliar environment.

However, these benefits come at a considerable cost. The most visible is the loss of diversity. Part of the pleasure of visiting another city lies in discovering its particular food, markets and shops, yet when the same brands dominate every high street, cities begin to look and feel interchangeable. More seriously, local businesses often cannot compete with multinationals that buy in enormous quantities and spend heavily on advertising. When a family-run bakery or bookshop closes, the community loses not only a business but also a meeting place and a piece of its identity. In addition, much of the profit generated by international chains is transferred to distant headquarters rather than reinvested locally, which weakens regional economies over time.

There are also cultural consequences. As global fast-food and fashion become the norm, traditional dishes, crafts and styles of dress may come to be seen as old-fashioned, particularly by younger generations, and eventually disappear.

In conclusion, while international brands provide convenience, reliability and employment, I believe their spread is largely negative, as it reduces cultural diversity and undermines local enterprise. Cities would benefit from planning policies that protect independent businesses alongside global ones.
models.commentary: Task Response (8): da una valoración clara ('on balance, a negative development') desde la introducción y la mantiene, tras reconocer con honestidad los aspectos positivos. Desarrolla tres consecuencias negativas (diversidad, comercio local, beneficios que salen de la región) y una cultural, con ejemplos concretos. Coherence & Cohesion (8): estructura sólida (concesión, argumentos principales, cultura); 'More seriously' marca una gradación muy eficaz. Lexical Resource (8): léxico preciso ('erodes', 'distinctive character', 'interchangeable', 'family-run', 'undermines local enterprise', 'reinvested'). Grammatical Range & Accuracy (8): estructuras complejas y variadas ('not only... but also', 'otherwise these companies would not have expanded', 'may come to be seen') sin errores. Para un 9: algún matiz más fino (p. ej., marcas globales que adaptan su oferta al gusto local) que demuestre una comprensión aún más profunda.

models.text:
In many cities around the world, people can find the same international shops, restaurants and clothing brands, such as McDonald's, Starbucks and Zara. While this trend has some advantages, I believe that it is mainly a negative development.

On the one hand, international brands have some positive effects. Firstly, they usually offer products of good quality at reasonable prices, and customers know exactly what to expect. Secondly, these companies create many jobs, especially for young people and students. For example, many university students work part-time in fast-food restaurants to pay for their studies. In addition, tourists and foreigners may feel more comfortable when they can find familiar food and shops in another country.

On the other hand, I think the disadvantages are more important. The main problem is that cities are losing their own identity. When every shopping street has the same shops, it becomes boring to travel, because many cities look almost the same. Another problem is that small local businesses cannot compete with big international companies, which have more money for advertising and can sell at lower prices. As a result, many traditional shops and restaurants have closed, and the owners and their employees have lost their income. Furthermore, local culture may suffer. For instance, young people may prefer burgers and pizza to traditional dishes, so these dishes could gradually be forgotten.

In conclusion, although international brands provide jobs and reliable products, I believe their spread is a negative development, because it reduces the variety and character of cities and harms local businesses and culture.
models.commentary: Task Response (7): postura clara y mantenida, con ventajas y desventajas relevantes y ejemplos (estudiantes con trabajos a tiempo parcial). El desarrollo es correcto pero algo predecible, y no explica por qué las desventajas pesan más que las ventajas. Coherence & Cohesion (7): estructura clara; conectores correctos pero mecánicos ('On the one hand', 'Firstly', 'Secondly', 'In addition', 'Another problem', 'Furthermore'). Lexical Resource (7): vocabulario adecuado ('reasonable prices', 'identity', 'compete', 'gradually be forgotten'), con alguna expresión informal ('it becomes boring to travel'). Grammatical Range & Accuracy (7): buen control (relativas, 'As a result', comparativas); errores casi inexistentes. Para subir a 8: justificar el juicio global (por qué la pérdida de identidad pesa más que el empleo), introducir un argumento económico menos obvio (beneficios que salen del país) y usar un registro más formal y preciso.

models.text:

prompt:
An increasing number of people now get most of their news from social media rather than from newspapers, television or radio.

Is this a positive or negative development?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
checklist: State clearly whether this is a positive or negative development (or mainly one or the other)
Consider the benefits of getting news from social media
Consider the drawbacks
Support ideas with explanation and examples
Keep the judgement consistent and restate it in the conclusion

for: News is instant, free and accessible on a phone anywhere
Ordinary citizens can report events and expose abuses (citizen journalism)
Users can access a wider range of voices than a few large media companies
Interactive: people can discuss and share stories
against: False and misleading information spreads quickly and is rarely corrected
Algorithms show users what they already agree with (filter bubbles), increasing polarisation
Headlines and short clips replace in-depth analysis
Traditional newspapers lose revenue, reducing professional investigative journalism

models.text:
For a growing proportion of the population, especially those under thirty, the morning newspaper and the evening television bulletin have been replaced by a stream of posts, videos and headlines on social media. While this shift has made news more immediate and diverse, I consider it a largely negative development, chiefly because of its effects on the accuracy of information and the quality of public debate.

The benefits should not be underestimated. Social media allows news to travel almost instantly, and it is available free of charge to anyone with a phone. It has also given a voice to people who were previously ignored by mainstream outlets: eyewitnesses can share footage of protests, natural disasters or police misconduct within minutes, sometimes forcing authorities to respond. In countries where traditional media is controlled by the state, these platforms may be one of the few sources of independent information.

Nevertheless, the drawbacks are more serious. Unlike newspapers and broadcasters, social media platforms do not verify what users publish, so rumours, manipulated images and deliberate disinformation can reach millions of people before any correction appears. The problem is compounded by algorithms that prioritise content likely to provoke strong reactions, which tends to favour sensational or divisive stories over careful reporting. Because these systems also show users more of what they already agree with, people may end up in 'filter bubbles', increasingly unaware of other perspectives and more hostile to those who hold them.

There is also a long-term economic consequence. As advertising revenue moves to technology companies, many newspapers have cut staff or closed, and expensive investigative journalism, the kind that uncovers corruption or corporate wrongdoing, is often the first casualty.

In conclusion, although social media has democratised access to news and amplified neglected voices, its tendency to spread misinformation, deepen polarisation and undermine professional journalism makes it, on balance, a negative development. Readers should therefore combine it with reliable, established news sources.
models.commentary: Task Response (8): valoración clara ('largely negative') presentada desde el principio y mantenida; reconoce con solidez los beneficios (periodismo ciudadano, países con censura) y desarrolla en profundidad los inconvenientes (verificación, algoritmos, burbujas, financiación del periodismo). Coherence & Cohesion (8): progresión muy clara; 'The problem is compounded by', 'There is also a long-term economic consequence' añaden capas al argumento con naturalidad. Lexical Resource (8): léxico rico y preciso ('mainstream outlets', 'footage', 'disinformation', 'divisive', 'filter bubbles', 'corporate wrongdoing', 'democratised'). Grammatical Range & Accuracy (8): estructuras complejas variadas (relativas, comparativas 'Unlike...', aposiciones) sin errores. Para un 9: un ejemplo concreto de desinformación viral o de periodismo ciudadano con impacto real reforzaría aún más los argumentos.

models.text:
These days, many people, especially young people, read the news on social media platforms such as X, Instagram and TikTok instead of buying newspapers or watching the news on TV. In my opinion, although this trend has some benefits, it is mostly a negative development.

There are some clear advantages to getting news from social media. Firstly, it is fast and convenient. People can find out what is happening in the world in real time, wherever they are, simply by looking at their phones. Secondly, social media allows ordinary people to share information. For example, during natural disasters, people often post videos and updates that help others understand the situation and find help. This can be quicker than traditional news.

However, the disadvantages are more significant. The biggest problem is fake news. On social media, anyone can post anything, and there is nobody who checks whether the information is true. As a result, false stories can spread very quickly and influence people's opinions, for instance during elections. Another problem is that social media apps show users content that matches their interests and beliefs, so people rarely see different points of view. This can make society more divided. Moreover, most posts are very short, so people only read headlines and do not understand complex issues in depth.

In conclusion, social media makes news faster and more accessible, but I believe this development is negative overall because it spreads false information, divides society and encourages superficial reading. People should still use reliable sources like professional newspapers to stay well informed.

El desarrollo es algo menos profundo: menciona las burbujas informativas, pero no explica el papel de los algoritmos en la viralidad, ni el impacto económico en el periodismo. Coherence & Cohesion (7): organización clara; conectores correctos pero formulaicos ('Firstly', 'Secondly', 'However', 'Another problem', 'Moreover'). Lexical Resource (7): vocabulario adecuado ('in real time', 'fake news', 'divided', 'superficial reading'), aunque con algunas expresiones generales ('anyone can post anything'). Grammatical Range & Accuracy (7): buen control de estructuras complejas ('whether the information is true', 'As a result'); errores mínimos. Para subir a 8: profundizar en un argumento (cómo los algoritmos priorizan contenido sensacionalista), añadir un efecto a largo plazo y usar léxico más preciso ('disinformation', 'polarisation', 'verify').

Nowadays a lot of people read the news in the social media like Facebook or Instagram and they don't buy newspapers or watch the news in the TV. I think this is a negative development for some reasons, but it has also some positive aspects.

The positive aspect is that the social media is very fast. When something happen in the world, you can know it in one minute in your phone. Also it is free, and the newspapers are expensive. Another good thing is that everybody can write the news, not only the journalists. For example, when there was a earthquake in my country, many people put videos in Twitter and everybody could see what was happening.

However, there are more negative aspects. The first problem is the fake news. In the social media there are many news that are not true, and many people believe them because they don't check the information. This is very dangerous, for example in the elections, because people can vote for a politician because of a false news. The second problem is that the news in social media are very short and people don't read the complete information, so they don't understand the problem very well. Also, the newspapers are losing money because people don't buy them and some of them are closing.

In conclusion, I think that read the news in the social media is negative because there are many fake news and the information is not complete. People should read also the newspapers to have the real information.
